title: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Announcer Jim Thornton Allegedly Visited Pedophilia Chatroom, Leading to Suspension
description: More details regarding the suspension of “Wheel of Fortune” announcer Jim Thornton are emerging: According to TMZ, the website has received photos f
body:
More details regarding the suspension of “Wheel of Fortune” announcer Jim Thornton are emerging: According to TMZ, the website has received photos from an American Airlines passenger who says they saw Thornton’s laptop opened on a “disturbing chat room” that appeared to be “images and texts that made it appear it was a chat room for pedophiles.”

	TMZ included several photos that the passenger supposedly took of Thornton’s screens, which include comments and texts that suggest inappropriate behavior toward minors, but those photos have not been authenticated.
	

	The alleged incident that led to the suspension apparently took place on an American Airlines flight in May. The passenger told TMZ that they informed a flight attendant about the chat room usage, and that authorities questioned Thornton at LAX when his flight landed. He was then given permission to leave, the website said.

	The news stunned Hollywood insiders who know and who have worked with Thornton, who generally has a positive reputation as a TV announcer and as a reporter. In Los Angeles, Thornton is known for his long-running roles in both radio, via KNX 1070 Newsradio and TV as a traffic anchor on KCBS-TV. (He is no longer with either station.) 

	Thornton’s lawyer, Allison Hart, has so far not returned requests for comment. But TMZ said she told the outlet that it was a misunderstanding, and that Thornton had “become active in suicide-prevention advocacy since losing a close family member to suicide two years ago and he has spent time visiting chat rooms offering support to individuals suffering from suicidal ideation.”
	

	The site, she said, is “not unlawful, there is no unlawful child pornography or other pedophilic content and my client never viewed, downloaded or consumed any child pornography whether on that commercial flight in May or at any other time. In short, my client did nothing wrong.”

	Thornton hasn’t commented on his suspension, and doesn’t have an active social media presence (his last post on X/Twitter was in 2016), so there’s been little information coming from his camp. The announcer also doesn’t maintain a website, it’s unclear if he is still set up at a talent agency (his last reps, A3 Artists Agency, shut down in 2024).

	The only confirmed detail in this situation came from Sony Pictures TV, which said Tuesday that “we have recently been made aware of allegations concerning Jim Thornton. He has been suspended from ‘Wheel of Fortune’ and we are recasting while we conduct a thorough investigation.”  

	TMZ, which first reported the suspension, previously wrote that “sources with direct knowledge tell us the pilot called ahead to have law enforcement meet Thornton when they arrived at the gate,” the site said. Thornton was wearing a “Wheel of Fortune” jacket, the site added, noting that he was questioned but “ultimately released.” 

	The announcer joined “Wheel” in 2010 after the death of the show’s previous announcer, Charlie O’Donnell, and has also worked as a substitute announcer on “The Price Is Right.”

	Thornton’s other credits include “Celebrity Deathmatch,” where he voiced Johnny Gomez, and as an announcer on “The Cleveland Show” and “Tim & Eric Awesome Show, Great Job!” He’s also been heard on several video games and appeared as a commercial narrator in the 2001 animated film “Monsters, Inc.” He also voiced the 2011 Oscar-nominated short animated film “Let’s Pollute.”

schema.headline: ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Announcer Jim Thornton Allegedly Visited Pedophilia Chatroom, Leading to Suspension

title: Maria Bartiromo vs. Fox News: The Anchor’s Pivot Between MAGA Politics and Wall Street Likely Spurred Fallout
description: Maria Bartiromo was brought to Fox to cover the ins and outs of Wall Street, and make the company a bigger presence in the world of business-news ca
body:
Maria Bartiromo was brought to Fox to cover the ins and outs of Wall Street, and make the company a bigger presence in the world of business-news cable. But her growing interest in punditry and opinion left Fox increasingly uncovered before the law.

	And that constant back-and-forth likely caused something of which a financial reporter is very aware: Her stock at Fox began to drop.  She has not been on the air since August 9.


	In June, Bartiromo read an apology on air after entrepreneur and “Shark Tank” personality Kevin O’Leary appeared on one of her shows a month earlier and made the false accusation that detractors of a data center he wanted to build in Utah were being funded by China. For executives at Fox News Media, it may have been the second-to-last straw.
	

	Bartiromo is believed to have passed along a directive issued to executive producers at Fox Business Network to the White House, according to a person familiar with the matter, and those instructions may have cautioned Fox Business staffers against support to outlandish claims made by President Donald Trump in public remarks. Divulging confidential company information to an outside party would likely be seen as a violation of terms of employment. 

	An attorney for Bartiromo, Bryan Freedman, railed against those details. “The irresponsible reports that have been published stating that Maria Bartiromo was fired or is no longer an employee of Fox are absolutely and unequivocally false,” he said in a statement Friday. “Make no mistake, we have the receipts and witnesses and they will come out whether through the courthouse or otherwise. Those reporting her firing or the incredulous facts supporting that fiction have exhibited a complete and utter reckless disregard for the truth. “ Freedman has represented news personalities including Megyn Kelly and Tucker Carlson after they had fallings-out, respectively, with NBCUniversal and Fox News.
	

	Fox News Media announced it had parted ways with Bartiromo Thursday, in a terse note that offered little explanation for cutting ties with one of the company’s best-known and most vociferous on-air personalities. A Fox News spokesperson called Bartiromo’s departure “a business decision.” Some details of Bartiromo’s actions were previously reported by Status, a newsletter focused on the media industry. Fox News declined to make executives available for comment.

	While Bartiromo had a regular Sunday-morning show, “Sunday Morning Futures,” on Fox News Channel,  where she often interviewed members of Trump’s Cabinet, her main job remained covering the ins-and-outs of Wall Street. She anchored hours and hours of markets and business coverage on Fox Business Network, both on her early-morning program “Mornings With Maria” as well as the Friday program “Maria Bartiromo’s Wall Street.”

	President Trump predicted backlash for Fox News following its decision. “I can’t believe Maria Bartiromo is no longer going to have her great show(s) on Fox News/Business,” Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social account Thursday evening. “Three different shows, always number one. Maria is a total professional, and a true warrior. Her fans, of which there are many, will not be happy. God bless you, Maria!”

	Her main business program, however, was not generating top dollar for Fox News, or its parent, Fox Corporation. Indeed, in recent quarters, “Mornings With Maria” attracted fewer viewers than its main rival, CNBC’s “Squawk Box,” according to data from Nielsen. More troubling, perhaps, is the show’s lack of pull among viewers between 25 and 54 — the demographic craved most by advertisers in news programming. 

	In the third quarter of 2026, “Mornings With Maria” captured just 5,000 viewers between 25 and 54, according to Nielsen, compared with 24,000 for “Squawk Box.” Bartiromo’s show for many months beat out CNBC in terms of the broader crowd watching, but since the start of 2026, “Squawk Box” has won a larger audience. In the second quarter, “Squawk Box” captured an average of 140,000 viewers, one of its biggest ratings wins in months.  “Mornings With Maria” lured an average of 123,000.

	Ad dollars earmarked for her shows on Fox Business Network fell to $3.7 million in 2025, according to data from iSpot, a tracker of ad spending, down from $8.9 million in 2022 — a decline of nearly 58%. Meanwhile, ad money supporting “Sunday Morning Futures” on Fox News fell to $6.1 million in 2025, according to iSpot, down from $7.8 million in 2022 — a dip of nearly 22%.
	

	Bartiromo’s penchant for politics has already cost Fox money. Bartiromo was one of a handful of Fox News personnel cited in materials tied a $1.6 billion defamation lawsuit filed by voting technology company Dominion Voting against Fox News in 2021. Fox ultimately agreed to settle the matter for a whopping $787.5 million. The allegations said Bartiromo had allowed false claims about the 2020 presidential election to air on the network as part of a bid to keep angry viewers from abandoning its program. She is also a defendant in a separate defamation lawsuit filed by Smartmatic, another voting-technology firm over false claims made on Fox the company played a role in affecting the outcome of the 2020 presidential election. Fox has said Smartmatic can’t prove that any reporting on Fox News properties caused it to suffer any financial harm.

	Parting ways with top talent brings with it the frenetic task of trying to replace them without surprising viewers further. Executives at Fox News may have more confidence they can navigate such issues, however, because they have done so quite well in the not-so-distant past. Fox News has managed through the departures of former primetime stars like Bill O’Reilly as well as Kelly and Carlson. 

	The company also has a set of very loyal viewers, who are willing to let Fox News run rotating anchors in an hour after popular personalities leave, and to give a chance to up and comers. Fox News largely re-set its primetime lineup in 2023 by putting Jesse Watters in Carlson’s former 8 p.m. time slot and moving Greg Gutfeld’s 11 p.m. program to 10. 

	Bartiromo may also have been seen as increasingly expensive in an era when traditional cable is in a battle for its livelihood with the appeal of cord cutting. Fox Business Network will still generate millions in revenue in years ahead, but, like others, is under pressure, according to Kagan, a market-research firm that is a unit of S&P Global Intelligence. Distribution revenue is seen dipping to $289 million in 2027, according to Kagan estimates, a dip of just 3% from $298.1 million in 2025. Ad sales are seen falling 11% to $55.6 million in 2025, compared with $62.7 million in 2005. And subscribers are declining, with Kagan projecting a base of 53.7 million in 2027, compared with 60.9 million last year.
	

	Talking about election integrity and data centers isn’t what viewers expected when Bartiromo initially signed on. Lured away from CNBC by former Fox News chief Roger Ailes — who had a hand in her early rise when he helped build the one-time NBCUniversal cable outlet. When she arrived at Fox more than a decade ago,  Bartiromo aimed to give business-news aficionados more than just stock quotes.  

	“There was a moment in time when it was really all about the stock market, and I know, because I was there,” she told Variety in 2014. ”I think today viewers want something very different.” People with an interest in business “want to know about the latest technology. They want the international story, the emerging markets. They want to know about jobs. They want to know more and expect more and deeper perspective. That really is my opportunity.” Given recent developments, Bartiromo may have squandered it.

schema.headline: Maria Bartiromo vs. Fox News: The Anchor’s Pivot Between MAGA Politics and Wall Street Likely Spurred Fallout

title: KJ Apa, Isabel May and Archie Renaux YA Romance ‘Falling’ Getting North America Theatrical Release From Brainstorm Media (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Falling,” the London-set romantic drama starring KJ Apa (“Riverdale”), Isabel May (“Scream 7,” “Mr. Irrelevant”), and Archie Renaux (“Alien: Romulu
body:
“Falling,” the London-set romantic drama starring KJ Apa (“Riverdale”), Isabel May (“Scream 7,” “Mr. Irrelevant”), and Archie Renaux (“Alien: Romulus”), is set to hit cinemas, having been acquired by Brainstorm Media for North America. 

	The Gulfstream Pictures film — from writer/director brothers James and Colin Krisel — will launch theatrically on Oct. 9, following by a Nov. 10 VOD release. International sales are being handled by Voltage Pictures.
	

	According to the description, “Falling” asks the question: What if the woman of your dreams was also dreamt by your best friend. “‘Falling introduces us to the anti-fairytale romance of an impossible love triangle between lovers and friends, set against the backdrop of endlessly inviting London locales,” it reads, adding that the trio of stars “confront the all-too relatable modern dating complication of preserving relationships while seeking self-fulfillment.”


	“We are thrilled to be working with Gulfstream again on another fantastic romance,” said Brainstorm CEO Michelle Shwarzstein. “KJ Apa, Isabel May, and Archie Renaux have a real chemistry on screen, and it’s exactly what makes this love triangle so fun to watch.”

	Added the Gulfstream principals: “We were thrilled to see this gem of a film find its way to a theatrical release with such a stellar cast of KJ, Isabel, and Archie – from emerging filmmakers, The Krisel Brothers.”

	Producers on “Falling” are Mike Karz and Bill Bindley of Gulfstream Pictures, Matt Luber and Lena Roklin of Luber Roklin Entertainment, Piers Tempest of Tempo Productions. Executive producers are Apa, Dakota Rosen and Tom Salentine.
	

	The project was financed by Gulfstream Pictures and Clerendon Road Productions. Gulfstream has financed a slate of titles picked up by Amazon MGM for worldwide distribution including current releases, “Pretty Lethal,” “Upgraded,” “One Fast Move” starring Apa, and “The Other Zoey” starring Renaux.

schema.headline: KJ Apa, Isabel May and Archie Renaux YA Romance ‘Falling’ Getting North America Theatrical Release From Brainstorm Media (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Alix Earle Rips Into ‘Toxic’ Alex Cooper in Fiery Statement on Feud: ‘The Way You Approach Business Is Disgusting. You Choose Money Over Morals’
description: Alix Earle has publicly commented on her feud with “Call Her Daddy” host Alex Cooper for the first time in the season finale of her new TV show “Ear
body:
Alix Earle has publicly commented on her feud with “Call Her Daddy” host Alex Cooper for the first time in the season finale of her new TV show “Earle Meets World.” Earle first began working with Cooper in 2023, launching her podcast “Hot Mess” under Cooper’s media network, Unwell. Cooper’s network dropped Earle’s podcast just two years later. Neither commented on the reasoning behind Earle’s departure, but the influencer hinted at conflict happening behind the scenes. 
	

	In April, Cooper called out Earle in a TikTok video where she accused the influencer of starting “fake drama” and alleged she was reposting passive aggressive videos regarding their feud, including one that compared Cooper to an “ambulance chaser.” 


	“There’s no NDA. No one is stopping you,” Cooper said in the video. “Stop hiding behind other people and just say it yourself. What’s the beef?”

	Earle never addressed her rift with Cooper, but she revealed a drafted text message she considered sending the “Call Her Daddy” host in her reality series. 

	“I wanted to write you directly and let you know I don’t like you. I’m not gonna fall for your bait of getting into a back-and-forth online, and I don’t think you want that either,” Earle’s message read. “You are manipulative and toxic. Go ahead and say ‘it’s just a business’ all you want, but the way you approach business is disgusting. You choose money over morals.”

	She added, “You took advantage of me at a young age in a new industry I knew nothing about. You are full of false promises, and ‘Unwell’ was a continuation of that. We had a call where you threatened me to not go to war with you, because you know how sick and twisted you are.”
	

	“Go ahead. Share this, use it against me, but you will no longer scare or trap me,” the message concluded. “You’re right. I may be petty, but I’m not malicious. If there’s one thing I learned from doing business with you, it’s to never do business with anyone like you.”

	It’s unclear if Earle ever sent the text message. When talking to her family about Cooper’s public call out, Earle revealed she had stayed silent because she was “scared” of the podcast host, who she says told her, “You don’t want to go to war with me.”

	Earle’s father and manager, TJ Earle, revealed his daughter’s podcast wasn’t given the same amount of resources as other Unwell projects, and Cooper’s support for “Hot Mess” started to fade with time. He also claimed Cooper stopped inviting Earle to events and parties. 

	“What I was thinking — which makes me so sad for me at the time — is I was so happy,” Earle said while getting emotional. “I trusted her so much, and all she did was just shit on it.”

	Earle also revealed she found out she was dropped from Unwell through the media and not from Cooper or her team. She also shared that during her 2023 appearance on “Call Her Daddy,” Cooper had Earle drink before filming the episode and then asked her sexually explicit questions, which made Earle feel “betrayed.”

	“I’m imagining myself in her shoes, to take someone in college who’s young, impressionable, you know looks up to you, and then ask them these raunchy questions,” Earle said on her reality show. “It’s stuff that I didn’t necessarily want to live on the internet forever.”

schema.headline: Alix Earle Rips Into ‘Toxic’ Alex Cooper in Fiery Statement on Feud: ‘The Way You Approach Business Is Disgusting. You Choose Money Over Morals’

title: Music Industry Moves: Wilson Pickett Estate Sells Publishing Catalog, Other Rights to Primary Wave
description: The estate of legendary soul singer Wilson Pickett has struck a partnership with powerhouse Primary Wave Music that will see the two parties work to
body:
The estate of legendary soul singer Wilson Pickett has struck a partnership with powerhouse Primary Wave Music that will see the two parties work together to promote the Rock and Roll Hall of Famer’s music publishing catalog, as well as share in his name, image, and likeness rights. Their efforts will include new marketing, branding, digital, and synch opportunities, as well as film & television projects. Further terms of the deal were not disclosed. 
	

	Pickett was one of the top R&B singers of the ‘60s and ‘70s with a battery of hits including “In the Midnight Hour,” “Mustang Sally,” “Land of a Thousand Dances,” and more.


	Of the partnership, Max Pickett said “Promoting my brother’s incredible legacy has not just been a responsibility; it has been a labor of absolute love. Wilson poured his soul into every lyric, leaving us a musical inheritance that belongs to the world. Since his passing, it has been my sacred mission to ensure that his voice continues to echo for generations to come. I am profoundly grateful to partner with Primary Wave—stewards who truly understand the weight of his history and the timeless power of his sound. Together, we are keeping the Wicked Pickett’s fire burning bright.”

	Primary Wave’s David Weitzman adds, “Primary Wave is honored to partner with Max Pickett and the Pickett family to help preserve and expand the legacy of one of the most influential artists in music history. Wilson Pickett was a once in a generation talent, an iconic soul singer, electrifying performer, and one of the defining voices of American music.”
	

	+ Young Thug’s YSL Records has announced a partnership centered on Grammy-nominated producer, singer, and DJ Yume and Mega Millions Music. According to the announcement the deal spans music, distribution, touring, and long-term artist development; Yume will join Young Thug on his New Generation tour, launching in September. TikTok’s SoundOn has also joined forces with the labels and will handle distribution for upcoming priority releases.

	“YSL has always been about pushing culture forward and giving artists the freedom to become who they’re supposed to be,” Young Thug said in a statement. “Yume has that energy — you can hear it, you can see it, and it’s global. Partnering with Mega Millions is about putting the right team and the right resources around her without changing what makes her special. We’re building something bigger.”

	+ Nashville-based singer-songwriter Maggie Antone has signed with Island Records. The singer released her debut album, “Rhinestoned,” independently in 2024 and made her in Grand Ole Opry debut that year.

	 “Partnering with Island feels so serendipitous, and though it’s bittersweet to no longer be an independent artist, I feel more independent than ever,” Antone said.

	+ HarbourView Equity Partners has struck a strategic partnership with Grammy-nominated producer David Kershenbaum to acquire his interest in producer royalties and related rights across master recordings, including Tracy Chapman’s “Fast Car,” “Baby Can I Hold You,” and “Talkin’ Bout a Revolution,” Joe Jackson’s “Steppin’ Out” and “Is She Really Going Out With Him,” Marc Cohn’s “Walking in Memphis,” and numerous other works. Fox Rothschild, LLP served as legal counsel to HarbourView in this transaction.

	“Throughout my career, I’ve had the privilege of working with incredibly talented artists to create music that has connected with listeners around the world,” said Kershenbaum. “HarbourView shares my appreciation for great songs and the creators behind them, and I’m excited to partner with a team that understands this body of work.”

	HarbourView founder/CEO Sherrese Clarke said, “David Kershenbaum’s career as an American music producer includes collaborations with artists including Duran Duran, Tracy Chapman and Joe Jackson, and recognition through more than 75 international awards and Grammys nominations. We’re excited to welcome David to the HarbourView family and to steward this catalog and the creative work it represents.”
	

	Tuesday, September 1

	BMG has announced its executive management team and strategic leadership council, following the completion of its merger with Concord.

	Working under the oversight of BMG’s board of directors, the executive team will be comprised of the following individuals:

	Bob Valentine, Chief Executive OfficerBjörn Bauer, Chief Financial OfficerSebastian Hentzschel, Chief Operating OfficerVictor Zaraya, Chief Revenue OfficerAmanda Molter, General CounselKent Hoskins, Chief Transformation Officer

	BMG has also established an 18-member strategic leadership council, comprising the six members of the executive management team and 12 additional senior leaders from across the company (listed below). 

	Tom Becci, Global Recorded OperationsAlberto Chullen, Corporate Development & InvestmentsSophia Dilley, Concord OriginalsSean Flahaven, Concord TheatricalsCeline Joshua, Global Marketing & StreamingNitsa Kalispera, Global Supply Chain OperationsJon Loba, Global Frontline RecordingsRuth Martinez, Human ResourcesKristal McKanders Dube, Corporate CommunicationsAlistair Norbury, Senior Creative Advisor to CEO Bob ValentineTom Scherer, Global Catalog RecordingsJim Selby, Global Music Publishing

	Further leadership appointments across BMG’s business and functions will be announced separately.

	Monday, August 31

	Japanese superstar singer-songwriter Yoshiki has signed a global distribution and publishing administration agreement with BMG through his record label, Melodee.

	BMG will provide global distribution for Yoshiki’s new releases, beginning with “Forever Love (Live),” his new collaboration with internationally celebrated vocalist Josh Groban. The agreement also encompasses his solo album “Eternal Melody” and X Japan albums released from 1993 onward, including the hit albums “Art of Life” and “Dahlia.” BMG will additionally administer his publishing outside Japan.

	Yoshiki said, “I’ve always believed that music has no borders. I’m now entering one of the most ambitious and creative chapters of my career, with new projects that bring together rock, pop, classical and contemporary music in ways I have never explored before. I’m thrilled to partner with BMG to bring this vision to the world. ‘Forever Love’ with Josh Groban marks the beginning-but this partnership represents something much bigger for the future.”
	

	“Yoshiki is a true global artist whose creativity, vision, and connection with fans transcend genres and borders,” said BMG senior VP Michael Kachko. “We are proud to partner with him at BMG to support and amplify this next chapter on a worldwide scale.”

	+ Concord Music Publishing has signed Israeli singer-songwriter-producer Noga Erez to an exclusive global publishing agreement. The company has also signed Erez’s partner and main collaborator Ori Rousso.

	The go-forward publishing agreement covers all future works as well as select key tracks from Erez’s catalogue, including “Stuck In Heaven,” “Bubbling,” “Penny Lame,” “Not My Problem” and recent single “I Love You” featuring Armani White.

	“Noga Erez is a force of nature and truly one of a kind,” says Adrian Hillekamp, director of A&R at Concord Music Publishing in Berlin. The music of Noga and Ori demands attention, their live show is beyond exhilarating and they keep innovating on every record. At the same time, they selflessly give energy, motivation and hope through their songs. It is a testament to their ability to inspire and a privilege for us to be a part of.”

	+ City of Hope, one of the largest and most advanced cancer research and treatment organizations in the U.S., has named Black Music Action Coalition president-CEO Willie “Prophet” Stiggers to the executive board of the Music, Film and Entertainment Industry group, Over the past five decades, the group has raised more than $180 million to support the organization’s work.

	“For more than five decades, MFEI has brought together people who have reached the highest levels of the entertainment business and want to use that influence for something larger than themselves,” said Kristin Bertell, City of Hope’s chief philanthropy officer. “Prophet is a natural addition to that tradition. He has built an extraordinary platform by bringing people together around issues that matter, and he understands the impact this industry can have when its leaders rally behind City of Hope’s mission to make hope a reality for all who face cancer.”

schema.headline: Music Industry Moves: Wilson Pickett Estate Sells Publishing Catalog, Other Rights to Primary Wave

title: Producers United Joins Bipartisan Push for Federal Film and Television Production Tax Incentive
description: Producers United is joining groups like the MPA and DGA to urge the nation’s lawmakers to back the proposed federal tax incentive for film and telev
body:
Producers United is joining groups like the MPA and DGA to urge the nation’s lawmakers to back the proposed federal tax incentive for film and television production to “protect American workers and foster sustainable careers.” The coalition of film and television producers released its statement at the start of Labor Day weekend, which “recognizes the contributions of American workers to the country’s strength and prosperity.”
	

	The push for a federal tax incentive to counter the increase in productions outside the U.S. in recent years gained steam Monday when President Trump renewed his endorsement of the idea and called for a bipartisan bill. The federal tax incentive is one of the rare initiatives that is supported by both Democratic and Republican politicians and in Hollywood. Trump dubbed the proposed legislation the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act.


	“Producers United offers its strong support of the White House’s urgent call for a meaningful federal tax incentive to bring film and television production — and the tens of thousands of jobs and businesses it supports — back to the United States,” the statement said.


	“A federal incentive that works alongside state programs, will level the playing field and refortify our domestic production ecosystem.

	“As Career Producers responsible for creating and managing these projects, we urge lawmakers on both sides of the aisle to act now to support an incentive that protects American workers, fosters sustainable careers, and ensures that film and television can continue to be made here in the USA for everyone’s enjoyment around the world,” the group’s statement continued.
	

	Charles Rivkin, head of the Motion Picture Association, offered his support after Trump’s statement, and the DGA has also been urging the studios to lobby for legislation.

schema.headline: Producers United Joins Bipartisan Push for Federal Film and Television Production Tax Incentive

title: Mellody Hobson Tears Up Talking About Why Husband George Lucas Was Unwilling to Compromise on Lucas Museum of Narrative Art: ‘I Saw Genius Work’
description: Mellody Hobson delivered emotional remarks about her husband George Lucas as the two hosted a “friends and family” preview on Thursday night at the
body:
Mellody Hobson delivered emotional remarks about her husband George Lucas as the two hosted a “friends and family” preview on Thursday night at the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles.

	“I watched George up close,” Hobson said, explaining that she missed the earlier part of his career (the couple began dating in 2006 before marrying in 2013). “I wasn’t there for ‘Star Wars.’ I saw genius work, genuinely work, and it was awe inspiring. And he was fanatical at times, but the thing about a fanatical person is they’re a fan. He was a deep fan of these illustrators in this work, and he wanted them to be represented, and I became a deeper fan of his.”
	

	Hobson teared up as she continued, “I was a fan already, but I saw something, the inspiration, the unwillingness to compromise, the determination, the lack of sleep, the lack of rest, the doggedness that actually taught me so much more than I ever could have imagined.”


Last night was exciting. I got to preview the new @lucasmuseum. What an incredibly massive and beautiful institution. Here, Mellody Hobson talks about bringing the museum to life after about 20 years with husband George Lucas.Mellody Hobson Tears Up Talking About Why Husband… pic.twitter.com/mj6Akq2p3o— Marc Malkin (@marcmalkin) September 4, 2026


	The museum, which features 1,200 pieces from Lucas’s private collection, has been in the works for about 20 years. Located in Exposition Park and designed by Ma Yansong of MAD Architects, the museum includes 30 galleries and two restaurants.



	

					Lucas Museum of Narrative Art
									Courtesy/The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art
	



	“I thought I was tough. I thought I was strong, I thought I had a will, and then I saw George, and I was like, ‘Oh, that’s why you could only do six of those movies,’” Hobson said. “Any more would have killed you.”

	The museum opens to the public on Sept. 22.
	

	“Thank you so much for being patient with us, the town, the community, everyone, as we were trying to get this all done,” Hobson said. “We are amazed that we’re limping to the finish line and the joy that we get out of this is seeing how people react to it, especially children.”

	Hobson opened her remarks by thanking the artists in attendance.

	“This has been a very challenging, amazing, emotional, unexpected journey that someone from Chicago who grew up the way I did never expected to have in her whole life and say, ‘Come to my museum,’” she said. “Those words don’t even make sense for me.”

schema.headline: Mellody Hobson Tears Up Talking About Why Husband George Lucas Was Unwilling to Compromise on Lucas Museum of Narrative Art: ‘I Saw Genius Work’

title: Dolly Parton Gets New Hollywood Walk of Fame Star After Original Was Vandalized Following Her Death
description: Dolly Parton‘s star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame has been replaced after the original one was vandalized following the country superstar’s death. P
body:
Dolly Parton‘s star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame has been replaced after the original one was vandalized following the country superstar’s death. Parton died of cancer on Aug. 25 at age 80.

	The star, which Parton received in 1984, is located at 6712 Hollywood Boulevard, and already had a crack along it before it was vandalized. As of Friday, Parton’s star is now fully restored and viewable.


	In a statement to Variety, Ana Martinez, Hollywood Walk of Fame Producer said, “Our Dolly is back! Hollywood is thrilled that her star is back in pristine condition for fans to enjoy forever. “
	



	

	



	The outpouring of support for Parton has been immense. Earlier this week, her estate announced the first large public programs honoring the life and music of the late superstar, with events titled “DollyFest: The Celebration of a Lifetime” set to take place in Nashville and London on successive weekends in 2027.

	Later this year, Dolly Parton’s “Dolly: A True Original Musical” is set to open on Broadway “as was Dolly’s wish.”

	In a statement to Variety, the producers confirmed, “As was Dolly’s wish, the Broadway production of ‘Dolly: A True Original Musical’ will begin previews Dec. 7 at the St. James Theatre in New York City with opening set for Jan. 19, 2027, what would have been her 81st birthday.”

	The musical will tell the life story of the country-pop superstar.

	Her music has also seen significant surges on Spotify. Following her death, total streams increased over 1,260% globally and 2,320% in the United States compared to the prior seven-day daily average.
	

	The country icon saw substantial boosts across her catalog after her death was announced. “Jolene” increased 630% globally and 1,225% in the U.S., compared to the prior seven-day daily average, while “9 to 5” increased 620% globally and 1,030% in the U.S. and “Islands in the Stream” increased 525% globally and 1,235% in the United States. “Jolene” was the most-shared Parton song on Spotify, followed by “I Will Always Love You” and “Islands in the Stream.”

title: Amber Eggers, ‘Love After Lockup’ Star, Dies at 41
description: Amber Eggers, who appeared in the 2019 season of WE TV’s reality series “Love After Lockup,” died Sept. 3 of acute liver failure at a hospital in Ge
body:
Amber Eggers, who appeared in the 2019 season of WE TV’s reality series “Love After Lockup,” died Sept. 3 of acute liver failure at a hospital in Georgia. She was 41.

	Her death was confirmed to TMZ by her mother Monica Eggers. 

	“Love After Lockup” follows couples meeting face-to-face for the first time after years of correspondence and visits while one partner was incarcerated. It documents the ups and downs of their relationships once they are released and together in person.
	

	Eggers, who was serving a four-year sentence for drug trafficking, was featured in Season 2 where her partner Vincent Gonzalez proposed to her on the show. Their relationship ended after her prison release. She made several cameo appearances in subsequent seasons of the franchise, including “Life After Lockup,” starting around 2021. 



	In 2025, Eggers’ health began to decline. Her sister Erin created a GoFundMe page announcing that she was hospitalized with severe pneumonia and a bacterial infection in her blood. The medical bills were putting a strain on her family, Erin Eggers said. 

	“I’m reaching out today with an update and a heavy heart to ask for your help,” she wrote in the post. “Many of you know Amber is one of the kindest and most big-hearted people you could ever meet. Right now, she needs all of that strength for the fight of her life.” 

	Over a year later, Eggers was hospitalized again “because she wasn’t feeling well,” Monica Eggers told TMZ. She added, “doctors couldn’t keep Amber’s heart beating any longer and she ultimately died from acute liver failure.

title: ‘Onslaught’ Director Adam Wingard on Adding Kink to His Movie, Why the Bad Guys Look Like ICE Agents and Spending ‘A Decade Slaving Away in the Studio System’ Making ‘Godzilla’
description: Adam Wingard‘s new movie “Onslaught,” in theaters Friday via A24, is an ’80s-inspired action thriller in which a combat veteran (Adria Arjona) has t
body:
Adam Wingard‘s new movie “Onslaught,” in theaters Friday via A24, is an ’80s-inspired action thriller in which a combat veteran (Adria Arjona) has to save her daughter (Blake Kennedy) when their trailer park is attacked by a trio of government-enhanced super soldiers. It’s a lean, mean throwback to the golden age of Cannon Films mayhem, and Wingard only has one regret.

	“I think the one thing I would probably do is add even more graphic violence,” he says.
	

	Given the ways the desert locals are treated as cannon fodder, it’s a wild request. But Wingard marvels at the amount of freedom A24 gave him for his R-rated siege tale.


	“It’s actually a relatively restrained film in terms of what you see,” he says. “There are a couple of moments of blood that are usually over the top, so that it’s not disturbing. There’s a lot of disturbing violence, but it’s usually not too gratuitous. I was really surprised … like the truck stop massacre sequence. I thought for sure we were going to get pushed back. I even expected A24 to push back on it, but we never had to censor anything in the film. I don’t know why that is necessarily. It might be a tonal thing, because the movie can tightrope walk fun and disturbing violence, but it’s not torturous.”

	The freedom to create his own world was a homecoming for Wingard, who made a name for himself directing a pair of indie hits: the 2011 darkly comedic slasher “You’re Next” and 2014’s down-and-dirty actioner “The Guest.” He used that momentum to tackle a pair of adaptations (2016’s “Blair Witch” and 2017’s “Death Note”), and then dove headfirst into megawatt blockbusters, helming 2021’s “Godzilla vs. Kong” and 2024’s “Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire.” 
	

	“After having spent a decade slaving away in the studio system and having reached this peak of what I was reaching for in my career with the last two ‘Godzilla’ movies, I felt like I’ve been waiting to get to this point where I can write my own ticket and get back to doing the types of films I think most represent me as a filmmaker,” Wingard says. “I knew the first chance I got, I thought I really want to do something that is almost capping a trilogy with ‘You’re Next’ and ‘The Guest.’”

	Although he has mentioned that “The Guest,” which stars Dan Stevens as a mysterious and violent soldier, and “Onslaught” exist in the same universe, Wingard sees an overarching theme running between the three projects, all of which have screenplays by his frequent collaborator Simon Barrett.

	“In a lot of ways, this film encapsulates both of those styles of movies,” he says. “‘You’re Next’ is essentially a siege movie that takes place mostly in one night, and ‘The Guest’ is much more a take on ‘Terminator,’ ‘Halloween,’ slasher films. We started looking at how to create a completion to a loose trilogy.”

	Additionally, Wingard became a father before developing the “Onslaught” story with Barrett, and it inspired a parenting throughline in the work.

	“My partner got pregnant while I was doing the last ‘Godzilla’ film,” Wingard says. “I was suddenly a dad, and this was a shocking new world for me. I also knew that the next film I was going to do was going to be something about a parent learning to be a parent. Knowing that really helped ground this wacky ’80s gonzo aesthetic, because I knew, ‘OK, I had this emotional anchor, and now I can go out and do all this crazy stuff, and we can tie it in to the worlds that we’ve already created.’”



	

					Rebecca Hall in “Onslaught.”
									Courtesy Everett Collection
	



	One gonzo element that will have audiences talking is a very kinky relationship between Stevens, who is nearly unrecognizable in a wig and makeup as an elderly German scientist, and Rebecca Hall as his dom. It’s a wonderfully quirky and kinky side plot that Wingard was thrilled to include.

	“Dan read the role, and this is our third collaboration together,” Wingard says. “The only note he had about this evil scientist character was, ‘I just feel like there’s something missing about him. He should be submissive to his wife in some sort of way.’ I said, ‘Oh, OK, I know what to do with this scene now.’ Suddenly, a lot of things changed in the movie after that, because I realized that we were making this film about not just surviving at a trailer park and being a parent, but it’s summarized by Michael Biehn’s line, ‘Let’s see what your pervert squad can do.’ These guys are the pervert squad, and we’re going to get in there; we’re going to learn about that Illuminati pervert squad.”
	

	From parenting to kink, there’s plenty brewing beneath the surface of “Onslaught.” Many filmgoers will also consider modern warfare, from the rise of unmanned drone strikes to the perceived AI arms race that politicians swear America could lose to its enemies. Even though Wingard didn’t intend for the film to feel so timely, he does say these issues are definitely simmering, starting with the basic conceit of the story.

	“By the time the movie’s done, you’re making something that was current a couple of years ago,” he says. “We knew we wanted to tell a story about PTSD, and there’s a shorthand to doing that with military, because we all understand that military equals PTSD no matter what. When you’re in those kinds of environments, it creates that. But there’s all kinds of different PTSD. That’s just how we’re taking that concept and putting it in the film so that it makes sense. But I was really blown away because everything was instinctual, and a lot of this film really does carry a heightened version of what my real worldview is in a lot of ways, especially the underground mechanisms of the military-industrial complex and secret programs and all those kinds of things. Even the lineage of us bringing Nazi scientists over from Project Paperclip from World War Two. I mean, those are all things that I believe in and are real. So this was an exploration of all those things.”



	

					Keil Zepernick, Alex Pereira and Steven Shelby Kekoa in “Onslaught.”
									Courtesy Everett Collection
	



	Wingard also inadvertently presaged the rise of controversy over increased presence of Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents, which echoed the super soldiers of “Onslaught” a little too well.

	“The whole situation with ICE … when we were making the movie, it really wasn’t what it became even six, seven months later,” he says. “I remember there were a couple of months where it was just nonstop ICE stuff. We were in post, and I remember one of the headlines: there’s this picture of four ICE agents. They’re all geared up with masks on, and they’re standing in front of some big vehicle with its lights backlighting them, and it’s a very dramatic shot. I thought, ‘Oh my God, this looks exactly like the shot of our killers standing in front of the truck in the movie.’ Horror movies always have to have a cultural significance for them to really work on some even subconscious level. We were just in the zone with the zeitgeist.”
	

	Watch the trailer for “Onslaught” below.

            10:50 AM PT -- The Massachusetts Supreme Court Justice has heard arguments from both sides, and will make a ruling ... and she says she'll do it pretty quickly. Stay tuned, because she could be back within just a few minutes.
      
    
            The Supreme Court of Massachusetts has agreed to hear Lindsay Clancy's argument to block the trial judge from declaring a mistrial, and we are livestreaming in the Supreme Court.
      
    
    
              
                
  
    
            Clancy's lawyer, Kevin Reddington, is trying to block the mistrial, arguing in part the holdout juror is not following the law concerning reasonable doubt ... at least so claims the jury foreman.
      
    
            The vote is 11 - 1, and although we do not know what specific charge is behind the vote, it seems somewhat likely the 11 may be voting not guilty by reason of insanity.
      

            The judge declared a mistrial, but agreed to let Reddington scurry to the Supreme Court, but the clock is ticking. The judge gave Reddington until around 2:30 ET.

title: 'Wheel of Fortune's' Jim Thornton: See Pedophilia Chatroom Photos Behind Suspension
description:
'Wheel of Fortune's' Jim Thornton
                          See Pedophilia Chatroom Pics That Led to S
body:
'Wheel of Fortune's' Jim Thornton
                          See Pedophilia Chatroom Pics That Led to Suspension
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 3, 2026
                
                            4:42 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 4, 2026
                                8:36 AM PDT
                                    
              
    
            These are the photos that got "Wheel of Fortune" announcer Jim Thornton suspended by the show and grilled by law enforcement.
      
    
            Thornton was on an American Airlines flight back in May from Charlotte to L.A. ... when a passenger eyed his laptop and saw him in a disturbing chatroom. The passenger tells TMZ, she saw images and texts that made it appear it was a chatroom for pedophiles.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            One of the messages she saw said, "Couple of cute boys and a hot little girl." Another read, "All-you-can-eat Boyfett." referring to a restaurant where they could find underage kids.
      

            And there's another message references "CP," which the passenger believed stood for child porn.
      
    
            As a result, the passenger notified a flight attendant and shared these photos with the crew. We're told the captain then notified authorities, and law enforcement met the plane when it landed at LAX.
      
    
            We're told authorities questioned Thornton and he was then free to leave.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Jim’s lawyer, Allison Hart, tells TMZ, Thornton had “become active in suicide-prevention advocacy since losing a close family member to suicide two years ago, and he has spent time visiting chat rooms offering support to individuals suffering from suicidal ideation.”
      
    
            The "Wheel of Fortune" announcer’s attorney said he often visited a suicide prevention website named 988lifeline.org and its chat forum, chat.988lifeline.org. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Jim claims he was sent a link to a different chatroom, lifeline.chat, from an acquaintance at the suicide prevention group. Lifeline.chat is for people with pedophilic thoughts ... and has no connection to the suicide hotline chat.
      
    
            The announcer claims he left the chatroom once he found out what it was, although from the timestamps it appears Thornton was in the room for at least 57 minutes.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            His lawyer added that website lifeline.chat is “not unlawful, there is no unlawful child pornography or other pedophilic content, and my client never viewed, downloaded or consumed any child pornography whether on that commercial flight in May or at any other time.” 
      
    
            Jim’s lawyer said their client was never arrested or charged with a crime. His lawyer claimed law enforcement spoke to Jim once he landed and determined no crime had occurred. “In short, my client did nothing wrong,” she said.
